outOfScope: Changing BB-065 objective in this allocation task.
Allowing ordinary RESEARCH_SA or WORKER PRs to redefine their own objective.
Rewriting historical objective/plan/evaluation artifacts or Git history.
Using supersession as product acceptance, delivery completion or dependency bypass.
constraints: This allocation remains a DRAFT research plan; exact publication schema and CI transition rules must be independently researched before READY.
Trusted-main objective/routing remains authoritative for ordinary Jev evaluation.
Supersession must be a separately recognizable publication with exact old/new objective and target-task bindings.
Target reset must revoke stale readiness/worker authority and preserve historical provenance.
BB-065 is the first intended migration consumer, but BB-082 must deliver the generic control before that migration is authored.
invariants: A task cannot evaluate a replacement objective that its own ordinary research candidate introduced.
Objective supersession preserves immutable prior evidence and never grants product or delivery authority.
A superseded unfinished task re-enters research with stale execution/readiness authority removed.
Downstream dependency impact is explicit and cannot be hidden by objective replacement.
architectureDecisions: Research the smallest explicit OBJECTIVE_SUPERSESSION artifact/publication shape instead of weakening candidateResearchTask trusted-objective checks.
Research a dedicated trusted CI path analogous to readiness publication but semantically distinct from Jev readiness.
Research atomic reset semantics for target objective/plan/lane/phase/status/claim/context/readiness bindings and downstream impact.
implementationSlices: R1 — Specify objective-supersession artifact, authority, freshness and impact contract.
R2 — Specify trusted publication validation and ordinary-candidate rejection behavior.
R3 — Specify atomic target reset, downstream staleness/impact semantics and migration provenance.
R4 — Implement controller/tests/docs only after Jev readiness.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A dedicated supersession contract binds exact target work, old objective, replacement objective, reason/evidence, plan and direct downstream impact.
Ordinary research evaluation still rejects any candidate objective/routing change; only the trusted supersession publication path may authorize objective replacement.
A valid supersession resets only an unfinished researchable target to DRAFT RESEARCH_SA/RESEARCH and clears stale claim/context/readiness/evaluation/worker authority.
Historical objective/plan/evaluation evidence stays immutable and exact supersession provenance remains reconstructable.
Downstream tasks affected by changed prerequisite semantics are explicitly identified/fenced rather than silently retaining stale execution authority.

researchGaps: Define the exact immutable supersession artifact/proposal fields and who may author/publish it.
Define how trusted CI recognizes and validates supersession without weakening ordinary objectiveRef/content trust.
Define downstream readiness invalidation versus explicit impact-only fencing when a prerequisite objective changes.
Define exact BB-065 migration procedure after BB-082 is delivered, including stale plan/readiness cleanup and retained historical evidence.
negativeVerificationCases: Ordinary research PR changes its own objective content or objectiveRef and still reaches Jev.
Supersession old-objective hash is stale or replacement objective does not match the declared digest.
Supersession preserves READY/WORKER execution authority or an ACTIVE claim/currentContextRef.
DONE task or unrelated task is reset through supersession.
Direct downstream tasks with semantic dependency impact are omitted.
Historical objective/evaluation artifacts are deleted or rewritten.
